rationale: My round-1 hard block CLEARS on my own re-derivation: every one of my round-1 repros now behaves honestly at ada49e53 (rebuilt binary, same fixtures and stateful bd stubs). F1 ADDRESSED: `--spec 999` / `--spec 042` / invalid `--spec` all refuse non-zero naming the resolution failure, in both the one-draft and zero-draft fixtures — never another spec's draft, never bare idle; ambient no-flag and full-ID draft targeting still work. F2a ADDRESSED: `--spec 131-active` with bd failing exactly its first call now prints {"mode":"plan","activeSpec":"131-active"} exit 0 (the recovered epic's real phase; the AC-1(i)-banned idle+activeSpec shape is dead on this path), and bd-fails-every-call refuses with the ADR-0035 recovery line. F2b ADDRESSED: the no-flag ambient flake also recovers to mode plan, not idle. F3 ADDRESSED: two drafts + `--spec 129` now propagates the correct "no spec found matching prefix" instead of the self-contradictory ambiguity advice; the no-flag ambiguity listing is intact. The valid-format-but-nonexistent full-ID pass-through refuses by name, and I audited derive.go to confirm an existing epic can never derive ModeIdle on the ResolveModeWithCache path, so that refusal cannot misfire on a real spec. G3's extend-reach works: a branch-only draft built in spec create's REAL shape (worktree add + commit + worktree remove, nothing in the main checkout's tree) is discovered from main as mode spec. Adversary sweep of the new code found ONE new issue, empirically demonstrated and cheap to fix (see ADV-1): FileExistsAtRef is called with the SHORT ref, so a same-named refs/tags entry shadows the confirmed branch in git's resolution order and silently flips a branch-only draft to {"mode":"idle"} — the exact misreport class this bead closes, and it defeats the helper's own documented exit-128 disambiguation precondition (the ref cat-file resolves is no longer the ref BranchExistsIn confirmed). Verified the one-line fix works: probing refs/heads/<branch>:<path> resolves correctly even with the shadow tag present. Everything else held: exit-128 empirics match the comment (present=0, absent-path=128, absent-ref=128); the branch-confirmation-first ordering IS enforced — FileExistsAtRef has exactly one non-test call site, resolve.go:261, strictly after BranchExistsIn; LocalBranchRefs failures propagate; garbage spec/ branch names (spec/UPPER_bad, spec/133) are idvalidate-skipped without disturbing discovery; the widened candidate set is epic-first-filtered (G6) so shipped specs cost zero git subprocesses; G4's instruct fallback to handleNoState is the disclosed bead-5-deferred disposition. Suites green from the bead worktree: internal/resolve, internal/gitutil, internal/instruct, internal/lint, and the TestStateShow legs (the five TestNextReadyGate host failures were proven pre-existing at parent f12ce273 in round 1 and are out of bead scope). Worktree left byte-identical at ada49e53. RC (no hard block) solely for ADV-1: a one-line hardening plus one test, squarely in this bead's honesty class.
concrete_changes_required: ADV-1 (NEW_ISSUE, MINOR) — internal/resolve/resolve.go:261 (draftSpecStatusWithCache tree-probe loop): pass the fully qualified ref to gitutil.FileExistsAtRef — probe "refs/heads/"+branch+":"+rel instead of the short branch name (or qualify inside the call site; either way the probed ref must be the ref BranchExistsIn confirmed). Empirical repro at ada49e53: branch-only draft fixture (spec create's real worktree-add+commit+remove shape) shows {"mode":"spec","activeSpec":"132-branchy"}; after `git tag spec/132-branchy main` (a tag on a commit without the draft — reachable in every clone via a normal `git fetch` if anyone pushes such a tag), the same command silently prints {"mode":"idle"} exit 0, because git's ref resolution prefers refs/tags for the ambiguous short name (git warns "refname 'spec/132-branchy' is ambiguous") and cat-file probes the TAG's tree. This defeats FileExistsAtRef's documented precondition ("an ExitError here unambiguously means path absent" holds only if the resolved ref IS the confirmed branch). Verified fix viable: `git cat-file -e refs/heads/spec/132-branchy:.mindspec/specs/132-branchy/spec.md` exits 0 with the shadow tag present. Add one test: branch-only draft + same-named tag pointing at a treeless-of-draft commit → still discovered as a draft.

findings.detail: Explicit --spec resolution failures now propagate (G1). Re-derived empirically at ada49e53: one-draft fixture — `--spec 999` → "no spec found matching prefix" exit 1; `--spec 042` → same exit 1; `--spec 'not_a_valid_id!!'` → validation refusal exit 1; zero-draft fixture — `--spec 999` → exit 1. Controls: no-flag single draft still renders {"mode":"spec","activeSpec":"129-foo"}; `--spec 129-foo` full-ID still works. The valid-format nonexistent full ID (`--spec 999-no-such-spec`) hits the new named refusal ("no active spec or draft found for 999-no-such-spec") instead of the R1.1-banned idle+activeSpec shape; audited internal/phase/derive.go — ModeIdle is never returned for a found epic on this path, so the refusal cannot misfire on a legitimately finished spec.

Both flake windows closed by the probe-then-rerun discipline (G2). Re-derived with the same stateful stub (bd fails exactly call 1, in_progress epic 131-active, spec dir+branch present): `--spec 131-active` → {"mode":"plan","activeSpec":"131-active"} exit 0 (F2a; was idle+activeSpec); no-flag → same mode plan output (F2b; was bare idle). bd failing every call → non-zero ADR-0035 refusal with recovery line. ResolveModeWithCache now health-probes and re-runs the epic lookup against the warm cache before any draft/idle conclusion; state.go re-runs target resolution after its probe.

Two drafts + `--spec 129` now yields the correct "no spec found matching prefix \"129\"" (exit 1) instead of the self-contradictory "use --spec to target one" advice; the no-flag multi-draft ambiguity listing is intact and pinned by G5 tests at both layers. Prefix resolution over drafts remains future work, as I conceded in round 1 — the honest refusal is the fix I asked for.

findings.title: Short-ref tree probe is tag-shadowable: a same-named refs/tags entry silently flips a branch-only draft to idle
findings.detail: draftSpecStatusWithCache calls FileExistsAtRef(root, branch, rel) with the SHORT name (e.g. spec/132-branchy). Git's ambiguous-short-name resolution prefers refs/tags over refs/heads, so a tag of the same name pointing at a commit without the draft makes cat-file probe the tag's tree: empirically, the branch-only draft fixture reports mode spec, then after `git tag spec/132-branchy main` reports {"mode":"idle"} exit 0 (git prints the 'refname is ambiguous' warning). The tag can arrive in any clone via a normal fetch. This breaks the helper's documented exit-128 precondition — the resolved ref is no longer the ref BranchExistsIn confirmed (BranchExistsIn checks refs/heads/ explicitly). One-line fix verified: qualify as refs/heads/<branch>; `git cat-file -e refs/heads/spec/132-branchy:<path>` exits 0 with the shadow tag present. Only the tree-probe leg is affected — dir-present drafts are immune.

findings.title: New-code sweep results: ordering enforced, exit-128 comment empirically true, union failure modes propagate
findings.detail: FileExistsAtRef has exactly one non-test call site (internal/resolve/resolve.go:261), strictly after BranchExistsIn returns true — the branch-confirmation-first ordering is enforced on every path today (worth keeping the doc comment's warning; a second caller would need the same discipline, and ADV-1's refs/heads qualification would make the precondition self-enforcing). Raw exit codes verified: present=0, absent-path=128, absent-ref=128 — the comment is accurate and the ordering load-bearing as claimed. LocalBranchRefs (for-each-ref refs/heads, pre-existing helper) propagates errors; DiscoverDraftSpecsWithCache propagates them (no fabrication). Garbage spec/-prefixed branch names (spec/UPPER_bad, spec/133) are idvalidate-skipped without disturbing real drafts (verified live). Widened candidate set is epic-first filtered (G6) so epic-having specs cost zero git subprocesses; branch-deleted-mid-probe TOCTOU reads as not-a-draft, which is the then-correct answer. G4's instruct handleNoState fallback on modeErr is the disclosed disposition (indeterminate-vs-idle in the tail is bead 5's stated territory). G3 extend-reach verified against spec create's real shape: worktree-add + commit + worktree-remove leaves nothing in the main checkout, and state show still discovers the draft as mode spec. Suites green (resolve, gitutil, instruct, lint, TestStateShow); the five TestNextReadyGate failures on this host were proven pre-existing at parent f12ce273 in round 1. Worktree byte-identical at ada49e53.
